rules.title: How to play
rules.board: The board: 3 rows, 15 lines (A–O). The middle square H2 is the Castle; D2 and L2 are X-marks.
rules.pieces: The pieces: 15 soldiers each (olbmát/gálgut), one queen (dronnet) each, and one shared king (gonagas) on the Castle.
rules.dice: The dice (birccut): X, II, III and blank. X counts as 1. You can always re-roll X faces by clicking the die itself — one at a time if you rolled several. Except when an activation is the only thing you can do (no pieces released), then you must activate instead. After a re-roll the normal rules apply to the new face, also if it is another X. II, III and blank are fixed.
rules.xmove: X releases the frontmost soldier in your row. You can also use X to move an already released piece one square (or your king/queen if they are in play). II/III move a released piece two/three squares.
rules.soldier: Soldiers only move forward in the cycle (your row → middle row → enemy row → middle row → home). They pass any pieces on the way, but can never land on lines where pieces sit that are not released.
rules.kingqueen: King and queen move straight up and down in the same column, and along the number cycle (the figure eight) — both ways. They may jump over pieces (only the landing is regulated), and cannot turn mid-roll. The king knocks out enemy soldiers and the queen (take the queen and you win), but cannot land on own pieces or on pieces that are not released. The queen captures like a soldier and captures the king.
rules.nesseby: Nesseby (optional, tick in the menu): the king cannot be captured by landing until someone has reached the opponent's home row — and the first soldier to get there captures the king for their side.
rules.landing: Soldiers capture enemies they land on. If you land on the king, you capture him. Your own soldiers may stand together on the same line.
rules.order: Order: use the X's first, then the III's, then the II's. If you cannot do anything legal with the current die, the rest of the roll is lost.
rules.win: Win: knock out the opponent's queen, or wipe out all of their soldiers (even if they still have the king).
